scope: Catalogue, plans, implementation/evidence review; no numerical rerun or full code audit.

issues.title: Loaded-wheel and suspension stations are not converged on bouncing; consider event location and error control
Footprint ring: an exact active-set solve is ~2x faster than projected Gauss-Seidel
Discrete outcome depends on exact float equality (photo-geometry label match)
Terrain requests: publish mandatory coverage first (a longer lookahead currently increases stalls)
Contact-driven runs branch at nanometre contacts; use sensitivity envelopes instead of fixed cross-platform budgets
Brake and traction creep under regularised friction: offer an exact-lock option or record the limit
Tyre casing: make hub-relative foundation damping an explicit material parameter
Bike rig stepping: implicit-Euler-type damping of the stiff tyre mode costs accuracy
Determinism: keep canonical numerics and integer ticks as the default; state the transcendental policy
Moving-wheel contact stiffness comes from the solver regulariser, not from the tyre
Moving wheel: large timestep sensitivity on rocks; report against an event-located run
Deformable wheel: the casing is not stiff for an explicit step; an explicit error-controlled step suits interactive use
Flex contact: the witness puts an edge's whole force on its deeper node; prefer a tread law continuous along the edge
Cheaper wheel tiers: judge them on rock corners against a converged nodal run (no modal cut-off in this casing)
Adopt the tiered CI strategy: local-first, smoke per change, full matrix at release
Canonical .5 records still branch between native and WASM MuJoCo on the trail preset
MuJoCo occasionally reports a flex-capsule contact with its normal reversed into the terrain
Engine solver tolerance limits per-step agreement on the light casing nodes (~1e-4)
Regularised friction cone: a locked wheel on an incline creeps at a measurable, predictable rate
Most tangential work on a rolling wheel is the regulariser's creep, not a rolling loss
Planar friction cone: an exact finite solve is available, and engine zone labels are unreliable near a boundary
Tyre rest: the settling failure is a limit cycle of the contact law at the level-edge tie, not the integrator
#54 direction: the sibling damping derivatives and the flat vertex contact don't address the rest failure
A rest test needs friction and a held brake (or rolling loss): frictionless and brake-free rest can't settle under a correct law
Cheaper and event-located wheel models fail at rest: include a rest run when judging wheel tiers
A held regularised brake lets a parked bike roll downhill at 0.14 m/s, well inside brake capacity
full_drive: the engine branches on its own collision tolerance after the drive releases
An edge lying along a terrain face has no unique contact point, so recorded forces depend on the collision routine
Smoothing a contact law per regime reintroduces a switch: smooth over one fixed candidate set
A smoothed contact law's band depends on the step, and the contact margin must be twice the band
